questions.question: Why did the Supreme Court say applying the new mail-ballot rules during the midterms would be “arbitrary and capricious”?
options: The Postal Service refused to enforce any election rules
Election officials lacked sufficient time to implement the changes
States had already finished counting mail ballots
Congress had prohibited barcodes on ballot envelopes
questions.explanation: The court found that election officials did not have enough time to reasonably implement the voter-list and envelope-barcode requirements. The Postal Service’s required online portal was not yet operational.

questions.question: What did House Speaker Mike Johnson confirm about Trump’s promised $5,000 payments to Americans?
options: Only federal employees would receive them
They had already been included in the federal budget
The Federal Reserve would distribute them
questions.explanation: Johnson said Congress must approve the payments and had not yet committed to them. Sending $5,000 to every U.S. adult could cost about $1.3 trillion.

questions.question: Who placed a hold on Trump’s proposed $2.8 billion arms sale to Israel?
questions.explanation: Rep. Gregory Meeks, the top Democrat on the House Foreign Affairs Committee, placed the hold over unresolved concerns about compliance with U.S. law and protections for civilians.

questions.question: How much did the Trump administration pay federal employees not to work during 2025 as part of the DOGE effort?
questions.explanation: The administration paid federal employees $9.5 billion not to work. Of that amount, an estimated $6.7 billion came from the deferred resignation program.

questions.question: How much did the Congressional Budget Office estimate the war with Iran would continue to cost each month?
questions.explanation: The CBO estimated that the fighting had already cost about $38 billion and would continue costing roughly $2 billion to $3 billion per month.

questions.question: How many articles of impeachment did Rep. Thomas Massie introduce against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth?
questions.explanation: Massie introduced eight articles accusing Hegseth of offenses including continuing the Iran war without congressional authorization and ordering extrajudicial killings.

questions.question: What did U.N. investigators find about the Feb. 28 U.S. strike on an elementary school in Iran?
options: The school was damaged by a strike on a sports complex
The strike was outside the mission’s jurisdiction
The school was the intended point of impact
U.S. forces had fully verified that the school was a military target
questions.explanation: Investigators found “reasonable grounds” to believe the school was the intended point of impact and said the failure to verify it as a military target went beyond negligence. More than 100 children were killed.

questions.question: What did Trump say were the only “guardrails” the artificial intelligence industry needs?
options: Voluntary standards established by AI companies
Independent audits of frontier AI models
questions.explanation: Trump rejected AI safety warnings as a “HOAX” and said the technology only needs a “STRONG AND SMART (High IQ!) PRESIDENT.”

questions.question: What benchmark interest-rate range resulted from the Federal Reserve’s quarter-point increase?
questions.explanation: The unanimous quarter-point increase raised the benchmark rate to a range of 3.75% to 4%, marking the Fed’s first rate hike since 2023.

questions.question: What notice must the Kennedy Center provide before making any major changes to its building?
options: Approval from the National Park Service
questions.explanation: U.S. District Judge Christopher Cooper ordered the Kennedy Center to provide at least 30 days’ notice before any major building changes. He also required a status report on its closure and emergency repairs.
